name: Reflex Volleys: One Attacks, One Blocks
summary: Close-range volley exchanges with fixed roles, one player punching hard and the other absorbing, to build reflexes and soft hands together.
setup: Two players across the net from each other, each two metres from it on the same side of the centre line. One is the attacker, the other the blocker. Basket at the net post. No bounces allowed.
instructions: Attacker starts with a firm volley at the blocker's body.
Blocker absorbs it and volleys back softly to the attacker's racket; the attacker volleys hard again, and so on.
Count the exchanges; a rally of eight banks a point for the pair.
Swap roles every two minutes.
Second round: the attacker may volley to either side of the blocker, not only the body.
coaching_points: Blocker: racket in front at chest height, elbows bent, and let the ball hit the strings; no swing at all.
Attacker: punch through the ball with the wrist firm; aim at the blocker's hip.
Both: eyes on the ball to the strings; at this range you cannot track the opponent.
Both: small split as the other player makes contact; the feet stay light.
progressions: Players move to one metre from the net.
Attacker volleys to the sides so the blocker must move.
No roles: both attack.
regressions: Attacker volleys at three-quarter pace.
Players stand at the service line.
Allow one bounce per rally.

name: Volley Direction: Cross or Line on the Call
summary: Trains volley placement off driven balls, directing each volley into a cross-court or down-the-line corner box on the feeder's call.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, driving balls with the racket. Volleyer on the near side two metres from the net on the deuce side. Two cone targets on the far side: a two-metre cone box in the far cross-court corner and a two-metre cone box in the far down-the-line corner, both against the baseline. Extra players queue beside the volleyer, outside the singles sideline.
instructions: Feeder calls 'cross' or 'line' as the ball is struck, then drives it at the volleyer.
Volleyer directs the volley into the called box.
Score two for the box, one for the correct half, zero for the wrong direction.
Ten volleys, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder calls only as the ball crosses the net.
coaching_points: Cross-court: contact further in front with the face angled; down the line: contact later with the face square.
Keep the punch short for both; direction comes from the face and the contact point, not the swing.
Step across towards the target with the opposite foot.
Racket head above the wrist for both, even on the low ball.
progressions: Shrink the boxes to one metre.
Feeder drives the ball harder from the baseline.
Feeder calls after the ball crosses the net.
regressions: Widen the targets to the whole far halves.
Feeder tosses underarm from the far service line.
Feeder calls before striking the ball.

name: Overhead Scissor Kick off the Deep Lob
summary: Adds the scissor-kick jump to the overhead so deep lobs can still be hit down instead of let bounce.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, lobbing with the racket over the player's head towards the near service line. Player starts at the near net, two metres from it on the deuce side. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline is the target. Extra players queue beside the player, outside the singles sideline.
instructions: Feeder lobs deep over the player's head.
Player turns, retreats with crossover steps, and hits the overhead with a scissor kick, jumping off the back foot and landing on the front foot.
Aim past the far throwdown line; score one for the far court, two for past the line.
Eight overheads, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder mixes deep lobs with short lobs; the short ones are hit without jumping.
coaching_points: Get behind the ball first; the jump is for reach, not for chasing.
Jump off the back foot, hit at the top, land on the front foot with the back leg kicking forward.
Free hand points at the ball until the racket comes through.
Hit down and through the ball with a full snap; a scissor-kick overhead pushed safe lands short.
progressions: Feeder lobs to the baseline.
Overheads must land in the far corner boxes.
Feeder follows the overhead with a passing shot to be volleyed.
regressions: Feeder lobs shorter so no jump is needed.
Player lets the deep lob bounce and hits it after the bounce.
Feeder lobs by hand from the far service line.

name: Poach Volley: Cross the Middle on the Feed
summary: Teaches the doubles poach, timing the move across the middle to the feeder's contact and finishing the volley at a target.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline on the deuce side with the basket, hitting cross-court drives as if returning serve in doubles. Net player on the near side two metres from the net on the ad side, in the doubles net position. A cone on the near centre line marks where the poach should be made; a second cone in the middle of the far ad service box marks the poach target. Extra players queue beside the net player, outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder drives a cross-court return towards the near deuce side.
Net player moves across the middle as the feeder makes contact, intercepts the ball at the cone, and volleys it at the far target.
Score one for a volley in the far court, two for the target.
Eight poaches, then rotate.
Second round: the feeder sometimes hits down the line instead; a net player who has already left the line loses a point.
coaching_points: Move as the feeder's racket meets the ball, not before; an early move gives it away.
Cross diagonally forward towards the net, not sideways along it.
Volley at a sharp angle or at the target's feet; the poach ends the point, it does not restart it.
After the poach, carry on through: land beyond the centre and hold the new side.
progressions: Feeder drives harder and lower.
Add a signal: the net player poaches only when a partner behind them calls 'go'.
Play the point out after the poach with the feeder alone.
regressions: Feeder tosses the return underarm from the far service line.
Net player starts on the centre line so the move is shorter.
Widen the target to the whole far court.

name: Volley-Overhead Combination: Two-Ball Feed
summary: Pairs a deep volley with an immediate lob to hit, so the net player learns to reset after the volley instead of admiring it.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, feeding with the racket. Player at the near net, two metres from it on the deuce side. A throwdown line two metres inside the far baseline is the target for both shots. Extra players queue beside the player, outside the singles sideline.
instructions: Feeder drives a ball at the player, who volleys it deep past the throwdown line.
Feeder immediately lobs; the player retreats and hits the overhead deep.
Score one per ball past the line; two balls, then the next player steps in.
Ten pairs each round.
Second round: the feeder reverses the order, lob first, then a drive at the player who has closed back in.
coaching_points: After the volley, expect the lob: keep the feet moving and the racket up.
Turn sideways on the lob immediately; the volley finish must not leave you square.
Volley deep, not hard; the overhead is where the point is won.
Close back to the net after the overhead as if a third ball were coming.
progressions: Add a third ball: a passing shot after the overhead.
Feeder lobs deeper so a scissor kick is needed.
Both balls must land in the far corner boxes.
regressions: Feeder waits until the player has recovered before the lob.
Feeder lobs shorter so no retreat is needed.
Feeder tosses the first ball underarm.

name: Swinging Volley off the Floating Ball
summary: Teaches players to take a slow floating ball out of the air with a full topspin swing instead of waiting for the bounce.
setup: Feeder on the far baseline at the centre with the basket, hitting slow, high, floating balls with the racket to land around the near service line. Player on the near baseline on the deuce side. A two-metre cone box in the far cross-court corner is the target. Extra players queue behind the near baseline outside the doubles sideline.
instructions: Feeder floats a slow ball that would land near the near service line.
Player moves in and takes the ball out of the air with a full topspin swing, a swinging volley, into the cone box.
Score two for the box, one for the far court.
Ten swinging volleys, then rotate.
Second round: the player follows the swinging volley to the net and plays a second ball fed as a volley.
coaching_points: Move through the ball: the contact is made while stepping forward, not from a stop.
Same swing as a topspin groundstroke, with the contact at shoulder height and out in front.
Brush up and over the ball; a flat swinging volley flies long.
Decide early: as soon as the ball floats, commit to taking it in the air.
progressions: Shrink the box to one metre.
Feeder floats the ball lower so the decision is harder.
Feeder follows with a passing shot after the swinging volley.
regressions: Feeder tosses the floating ball by hand from the far service line.
Widen the target to the whole far half.
Player may let the ball bounce and hit it on the rise instead.

name: Net vs Baseline Points: Win It in Three
summary: Live points between a net player and a baseliner where the net player must finish within three shots or lose the point.
setup: One player at the near net, two metres from it on the centre line; the other on the far baseline at the centre mark. Basket at the net post. The baseline player starts each point with a self-drop drive; the singles lines are the boundaries.
instructions: Baseline player starts the point with a drive at the net player.
Net player must win the point within three volleys or overheads; if the rally goes past three, the baseline player wins the point.
The baseline player may lob, pass or drive; the net player may not let the ball bounce.
First to eleven, then swap roles.
Second game: the net player must win within two shots.
coaching_points: First volley deep to the baseliner's backhand, second volley to the open court: that is the three-shot plan.
Split step on every contact by the baseliner, especially when you think the point is won.
On the lob, turn and hit the overhead; do not let it bounce even when tempted.
Baseliner: the low dipping ball at the net player's feet is worth more than a pass.
progressions: Net player must win within two shots.
Baseliner gets one free lob per point that the net player must let bounce.
Play games to fifteen with the net player starting from the service line.
regressions: Net player may win within five shots.
Baseliner may not lob.
Cooperate for two balls before the point goes live.

name: Volley Touch Ladder: Drop, Angle, Deep
summary: Three volleys in a row to three different targets, a drop, an angle and a deep ball, so touch and direction are trained from one ready position.
setup: Feeder on the far service line at the centre with the basket, hitting medium-pace balls with the racket. Volleyer on the near side two metres from the net on the deuce side. Three targets on the far side: a hoop a metre behind the net straight ahead for the drop, a cone in the far alley level with the service line for the angle, and a two-metre cone box in the far cross-court corner for the deep volley. Extra players queue beside the volleyer, outside the singles sideline.
instructions: Feeder feeds three balls in a row; the volleyer plays a drop volley into the hoop, an angled volley past the alley cone, and a deep volley into the corner box, in that order.
Score one per target hit; three balls, then rotate.
After everyone has had three rounds, the feeder calls the order at random.
Fourth round: the volleyer calls their own shot before each feed.
Finish with three balls where all three must be hit from the backhand side.
coaching_points: Drop: soft hands and an open face, the racket gives on contact.
Angle: contact well in front with the face turned early; the ball crosses the net low and wide.
Deep: firm wrist, short punch through the ball, finish pointing at the box.
Same ready position for all three; the difference is decided in the last half metre.
progressions: Shrink the deep box to one metre and move the angle cone further back.
Feeder drives harder from the far baseline.
Feeder calls the shot after the ball crosses the net.
regressions: Feeder tosses underarm instead of hitting with the racket.
Two targets only: drop and deep.
Widen all targets: the far service box for the drop, the alley for the angle, the far half for the deep volley.
